article_content: A popular app called Secret, marketed as a safe space for anonymous confessions, has been exposed as far less secure than advertised. Users sign up using just their phone number, email, or Facebook account—and once inside, they can view and comment on secrets shared by friends and even friends of friends, thanks to an algorithm that maps social connections. But what makes this system risky? Ethical hackers Benjamin Caudill and Bryan Seely discovered a way to unmask identities by flooding their own contact lists with fake profiles while keeping just one real account. Any secret posted by someone connected to that single real profile could then be traced directly back to them. In one test, they even uncovered a post from Secret’s own CEO, David Byttow, asking, 'Is Lucy the cutest dog?' Though some messages are playful—like admitting excitement over a new Taylor Swift song—the implications are serious. When users think they’re speaking anonymously, they may reveal deeply personal information. Byttow himself admitted the app doesn’t promise total anonymity. This isn’t an isolated issue: similar privacy failures have already led to regulatory action against Snapchat, which was fined for misleading users about disappearing photos. The truth? If your secrets rely on an app’s algorithm to protect them, they might not be secrets for long.

article_content: Tonight at 5:30 PM GMT, viewers across the UK can tune in to an unusual live television experience: a nine-hour marathon of knitting, broadcast directly from Norway. The event, organized by public broadcaster NRK, isn't just about cozy sweaters—it’s also an attempt to break the world record for turning raw sheep wool into a finished jumper in the fastest time ever. The current record—4 hours and 51 minutes—is held by Australia, and Norway’s team of skilled crafters aims to beat it. Before the big challenge kicks off, audiences will enjoy four hours of soothing, step-by-step knitting instruction, perfect for unwinding after a long day. This isn’t random entertainment; it’s part of Norway’s long-running 'Slow TV' phenomenon, which began in 2009 with a seven-hour live stream of a train ride from Bergen to Oslo. Back then, NRK staff thought it might be a quirky, low-cost experiment. Instead, it became a national sensation—people tuned in not for drama, but for peace. Since then, NRK has aired everything from a 379-hour boat voyage to a 12-hour fire being meticulously built. One producer, Rune Møklebust, admits he was skeptical when the knitting show aired on a Friday night competing with reality TV giants—but viewers stayed. Many wrote in saying they’d planned to watch for just a minute… and ended up glued to their screens for hours. Sociologist Arve Hjelseth explains why: in today’s hyper-connected, fast-paced world, Slow TV offers a rare pause. For Norwegians, watching a sheep being sheared or a train glide past fjords isn’t boring—it’s a comforting return to nature, silence, and simplicity. And now, thanks to livestreaming, anyone with internet access can join in.

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) — Two former coaches have sued Major League Soccer team Chivas USA, alleging they were fired this year because they are not Latino. Daniel Calichman and Theothoros Chronopoulos, who worked in the team’s academy — its player development program — claim team owner Jorge Vergara Madrigal of Mexico implemented a Latino-only employment policy, according to a lawsuit filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court. Calichman and Chronopoulos, both white and former professional players with ties to the U.S. national team, accuse Vergara of replicating a discriminatory practice reportedly used by Chivas de Guadalajara, a Mexican club owned by Vergara that has historically hired only Mexican players since its founding in 1908. The two men, seeking unspecified damages for discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and wrongful termination, say the team fired them 'as part of an ethnocentric policy and practice of discriminating against and terminating non-Mexican and non-Latino employees.' In a November staff meeting, Calichman recalled, Vergara asked everyone who spoke Spanish to raise their hand. 'There was a group that could not speak Spanish,' Calichman said. 'The work environment changed. Coaches who didn’t speak Spanish began wondering, 'Will we be fired because I can’t speak Spanish?' It feels horrible.' Chivas USA, which shares a stadium in Carson with the Los Angeles Galaxy, declined to comment. 'We are not commenting because it’s a legal matter,' said spokeswoman Christina Maillo-Belda. Co-defendant Insperity Inc., a Texas-based HR firm, also declined to comment, stating it had not yet been served or reviewed the lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges the coaches faced retaliation after reporting concerns to internal HR and the California Department of Fair Employment and Housing. They were terminated on March 7 and received a letter accusing them of unprofessional conduct creating an unsafe work environment — claims they dispute. Chronopoulos served as director of the academy, overseeing players aged 18 and under. Calichman reported to him, coaching 17- and 18-year-olds and assisting the senior team as needed. Both joined Chivas USA in August 2011. A year later, Vergara and his wife, Angelica Fuentes, became sole owners. The lawsuit claims Vergara undertook a systematic effort to reverse what he saw as the 'Americanization' of Chivas USA and impose a Mexican-centric model akin to Chivas de Guadalajara. Court documents cite Vergara’s public remarks calling Chivas USA 'the son of Chivas de Guadalajara' but noting the clubs had undergone a 'divorce in philosophy and structure.' According to the suit, Vergara replaced non-Latino staff and players with those of Mexican or Latino heritage — or those connected to Mexico, such as spouses of Mexican nationals. In December 2012, Chronopoulos was ordered to collect ethnic and national origin data from academy players’ families; many parents refused, offended by the request. Since Vergara assumed control, approximately seven non-Latino academy employees — including Calichman and Chronopoulos — have been terminated, the suit says. 'No Latino employees have been terminated,' it adds. The team has also nearly eliminated non-Latino players, replacing them with Latino players, according to the lawsuit and a Los Angeles Times report. Among those released or traded: James Riley, Ben Zemanski, Casey Townsend, and eight-time MLS All-Star Shalrie Joseph. The team acquired Eric Avila from Colorado Rapids in exchange for Nick LaBrocca, and brought in three players from Chivas de Guadalajara: Edgar 'El Chore' Mejía, defender Mario de Luna, and forward Giovani Casillas. As of Wednesday, Chivas USA ranked last in the Western Conference with a 3-7-2 record.

article_content: When Roy Keane took over as manager of Ipswich Town in 2009, he didn’t just focus on tactics — he had a very specific gripe about the team’s kit. The club’s traditional blue shirts bothered him, not because of aesthetics, but because of what they represented. To Keane, blue was inextricably tied to Rangers and Manchester City — two clubs deeply connected to his lifelong allegiances. As a boyhood Celtic fan and former Manchester United captain, he found the association jarring, even unsettling. So he did something unusual: he went to owner Marcus Evans and asked if they could switch colors. Evans politely declined, warning that changing the kit would spark major backlash. Keane, ever the wit, quipped that ‘uproar’ at Ipswich meant maybe four locals marching down the street with signs. In his memoir, The Second Half, he admits the whole thing sounds childish — and he doesn’t deny it. But for him, football isn’t just about results; it’s about identity, memory, and the deep, sometimes irrational, loyalties that shape a fan’s soul. Now assistant manager for both the Republic of Ireland and Aston Villa, Keane says he’d consider managing again — though he’ll probably still avoid blue.

article_content: It was a mission that captivated audiences worldwide — and now images have revealed the dramatic moment Orion was safely recovered into the well deck of the USS Anchorage. A combined U.S. Navy and NASA team successfully towed the spacecraft out of the water after a flawless launch and landing. Orion — which will one day carry astronauts to an asteroid and ultimately Mars — will be transported back to shore later today. On December 5, a joint U.S. Navy and NASA team recovered Orion safely onto the USS Anchorage. This marked the first at-sea test of the Orion Crew Module using a Navy well-deck recovery method. 'This mission exemplifies the U.S. Navy’s commitment to researching and developing technologies and techniques to ensure the safety of human spaceflight,' said Captain Michael McKenna, commanding officer of the USS Anchorage. 'I could not be more proud of my crew.' The successful retrieval of Exploration Flight Test 1 (EFT-1) was part of a U.S. government interagency effort to test recovery techniques for future space missions. Although this was Orion’s first trip to space, it was the fifth at-sea test of a module using the Navy well-deck recovery method — though previous tests used mock-ups. Four preparatory tests were conducted prior to the flight to train the recovery team and ensure operational readiness. The first test occurred at Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia, in August 2013. Subsequent tests, known as Underway Recovery Tests (URTs), took place earlier in 2014. Navy personnel worked as NASA’s Orion space capsule was prepared for unloading at Naval Base San Diego, California. Sailors from the amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage and Navy divers from Explosive Ordnance Disposal Mobile Unit 11 (EODMU11) attached lines to the Orion Crew Module. Divers surrounded the capsule — wearing green helmets — as recovery operations began. Airbags, inflated to maintain the capsule in an upright 'Stable 1' position, were visible. The USS Anchorage was selected for EFT-1 due to its combination of capabilities: a well deck, advanced medical facilities, helicopters, 3D air-search radar, and small boats — all essential for recovery operations. A specially trained bridge team supported the mission throughout. After Orion splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Baja California, the USS Anchorage maneuvered close, accompanied by small boats, to safely retrieve the capsule. Navy divers guided the capsule using towing lines, while a NASA-designed winch hauled it into the well deck. 'Orion is meant to be reused, which is why we tailored this recovery to keep the capsule safe,' said Navy Diver 1st Class Matthew Demyers of EODMU11. Chief Boatswain’s Mate Jason B. Roberts, deck department leading chief petty officer, added: 'We practiced this recovery many times with safety as the number-one priority. The sailors were focused and completed the mission successfully. I couldn’t be more proud of our sailors and the work they accomplished today.' During re-entry, Orion endured speeds of 20,000 mph (32,000 km/h) and temperatures nearing 2,200°C (4,000°F). In 11 minutes, it decelerated to 20 mph (32 km/h) at splashdown, aided by eight sequentially deployed parachutes. Cameras onboard captured the entire mission, including stunning views of Earth during re-entry and the fiery heat shield glow. The spacecraft passed through the Van Allen belts twice, experiencing intense radiation, and reached an altitude of 3,600 miles — more than 14 times higher than the International Space Station. Orion flew farther and faster than any human-rated spacecraft since the Apollo program. It landed precisely 275 miles (442 km) west of Baja California, achieving its target with remarkable accuracy. 'There’s your new spacecraft, America,' said Mission Control commentator Rob Navias as Orion neared the water. He called the journey 'the most perfect flight you could ever imagine.' If astronauts had been onboard, they would have experienced a peak g-force of 8.2 — nearly double that of a Soyuz return from the ISS. Three of five airbags deployed correctly — sufficient to keep the capsule upright. The mission was deemed a complete success by NASA leadership. 'Today’s flight test of Orion is a huge step for NASA and a critical part of our work to pioneer deep space on our Journey to Mars,' said NASA Administrator Charles Bolden. 'The teams did a tremendous job putting Orion through its paces in the real environment it will endure as we push the boundaries of human exploration.' After being offloaded at San Diego, Orion will be transported by truck to Kennedy Space Center, with officials hoping for arrival by Christmas. Orion is being developed alongside the Space Launch System (SLS), scheduled for its maiden launch in 2018 or 2019. Together, SLS and Orion will enable human missions to deep-space destinations such as Mars. The earliest possible crewed mission is targeted for 2021, with an asteroid mission planned for the 2020s and a Mars mission envisioned for the 2030s.

Durante il rientro, Orion ha sopportato velocità di 20.000 miglia all'ora (32.000 km/h) e temperature vicine a 2.200°C (4.000°F). Orion ha volato più lontano e più veloce di qualsiasi navicella progettata per esseri umani dal programma Apollo. È atterrata precisamente a 275 miglia (442 km) a ovest della Baja California, raggiungendo con notevole accuratezza il punto obiettivo. 'Le squadre hanno fatto un lavoro eccezionale mettendo Orion alla prova nell'ambiente reale che dovrà affrontare mentre spingiamo i confini dell'esplorazione umana nei prossimi anni.' Dopo lo scarico a San Diego, Orion verrà trasportata su camion fino al Centro Spaziale Kennedy, con l'obiettivo di arrivare entro Natale. Orion viene sviluppata insieme al razzo più potente al mondo, lo Space Launch System (SLS), il cui lancio inaugurale è previsto per il 2018 o il 2019. article_content: CNN) — A new job platform has emerged with the potential to assist hundreds of thousands of unemployed Americans navigating a sluggish economy. The website, located at www.universe.jobs and recently expanded by the DirectEmployers Association, serves as a centralized hub for job listings, offering a unified, one-stop solution for both employers and job seekers. What sets this initiative apart from established platforms like Monster.com and CareerBuilder? On those sites, employers pay significant fees to reach a wider audience. In contrast, the .jobs domain is completely free for businesses of all sizes. According to Tom Embrescia of Employ Media — the licensed operator of the .jobs domain — the goal is to create 'a trusted, valuable source where job seekers and employers can connect seamlessly under one intuitive URL.' Here’s how it works: Companies build their own dedicated pages on the .jobs domain, with listings updated daily. Job seekers can search by location or industry using specific subdomains. For example, someone looking for work in Boston would visit www.boston.jobs; someone seeking tech roles would go to www.technology.jobs. Any city with a population of 5,000 or more is eligible for its own subdomain. As of the end of January, approximately 40,000 .jobs domains were active through universe.jobs. According to Bill Warren, executive director of DirectEmployers — a nonprofit HR consortium — 580 Fortune 1000 companies are already actively posting jobs on the platform. Job seekers benefit from knowing these listings come from a 'highly trusted source,' where duplicates, scams, and expired postings are minimized, Warren said. Listings are updated at least once daily, and 41 U.S. states are currently represented. Programmers plan to eventually expand the platform globally. Major corporations are embracing the model. Providence Health Services, a nonprofit healthcare provider in Alaska, Washington, Montana, Oregon, and California, sees it as a way to reach beyond traditional candidate pools, according to spokesperson Rhonda Stickley. Brandy Ellis, a recruiter at Colorado-based Level 3 Communications, an IP transit network provider, noted that companies no longer simply post openings and wait for applicants. 'We’re now building talent pools — even if someone isn’t right for a current role, they might be perfect in the future. We’re changing how we think about job seekers,' Ellis said.

article_content: At the globally televised memorial for Nelson Mandela, sign language interpreter Thamsanqa Jantjie became the center of intense controversy. While millions watched world leaders pay tribute, viewers were stunned by Jantjie’s performance — critics described his hand movements as incoherent and lacking the facial expressions vital to South African Sign Language. The Deaf Federation of South Africa swiftly condemned him as a 'fake interpreter,' stating he is unknown within the local Deaf community and has no recognized credentials. Yet Jantjie insists he is fully qualified, pointing to years of experience interpreting at high-profile events and claiming no formal complaints had been lodged against him before. He shared that he lives with schizophrenia, a condition he manages with treatment, and said being selected for Mandela’s memorial was a lifelong dream. Meanwhile, South Africa’s Deputy Minister for People with Disabilities, Hendrietta Bogopane-Zulu, acknowledged the government’s failure in vetting procedures. She confirmed Jantjie held official accreditation but emphasized that South Africa has no unified national standard for sign language interpretation, leaving room for missteps. Adding to the confusion, the company Jantjie claimed to work for — SA Interpreters — reportedly disappeared after authorities tried to contact them. The ANC clarified it did not hire Jantjie; the state was responsible. Still, questions linger: How was someone with such visibly flawed interpretation skills approved? And why did no one raise concerns until now?

La Federazione dei Sordi del Sudafrica lo ha immediatamente condannato come un 'interprete falso', affermando che non è conosciuto nella comunità sorda locale e non possiede credenziali riconosciute. article_content: Lab-grown blue and colorless diamond jewelry by Valquère, the new division of the Baunat Group. Antwerp-based diamond innovator Baunat has launched a lab-grown diamond division alongside its existing ethical natural diamond business, becoming the first company of its kind to offer both natural and lab-grown diamonds — targeting two distinct customer segments. The Baunat Group’s new lab-grown arm, Valquère, will also offer technically complex fancy-colored blue and pink diamonds, uniting science, art, and traditional European craftsmanship in a thoughtfully designed collection. Located in the heart of Antwerp’s historic Diamond District, Baunat was founded in 2008 by diamantaires Stefaan Mouradian and Steven Boelens, offering high-quality, certified ethical natural diamonds with a short and transparent supply chain. Crucially, Baunat’s business model is demand-driven, not trend-driven, allowing the team to focus on the highly lucrative engagement and white diamond markets, where 60% of customers purchase bespoke or semi-bespoke pieces. Blending a digital-first, direct-to-consumer approach, Baunat has become Europe’s leading online jeweler over the past decade. A white gold ring featuring a 2-carat pear-shaped fancy blue lab-grown diamond, designed by Valquère. Customers can browse extensive style libraries on the Baunat and Valquère websites and purchase ready-made, semi-tailored, or fully bespoke jewelry, with production lead times of two to five weeks in the Group’s workshops in Antwerp and Paris. Baunat was ideally positioned to capitalize on the e-commerce surge during the COVID-19 pandemic, and 65% of its sales remain online today. 'Buying a jewel should be an experience,' says Mouradian. 'That’s why we’ve assembled a carefully selected team fluent in over 20 languages to serve clients worldwide.' 'Valquère is aiming high — we offer seven currencies and even cryptocurrency as payment options.' This launch coincides with a slump in the natural diamond market, driven by rising competition from lab-grown diamonds and global instability, which has disrupted rough diamond supplies from certain countries and suppliers. Rapaport reported 'market stabilization amid drop in rough supply' on November 9, 2023, as reduced production eases inventory pressures. Analysts will closely monitor the natural diamond market in the coming months, particularly as India prepares for a prolonged Diwali shutdown and geopolitical tensions persist. Existing Baunat customers are predominantly men purchasing for women, though an increasing number of women are self-gifting, especially in categories like tennis bracelets. Under the bold tagline 'Statement Made,' Valquère offers handcrafted artisan jewelry made with recycled metals and top-grade lab-grown diamonds, designed to attract consumers seeking aspirational, larger, and bolder stones at accessible prices. Most Valquère pieces fall within the €1,500–€4,000 range, with select pieces exceeding €10,000. 'Natural diamonds come with a premium price tag,' says Boelens. 'With the steady rise in lab-grown diamond quality over recent years, this luxury is now attainable for those who desire the traditional look — but with a smarter approach.' 'With Valquère, you can get a larger carat weight at a much more attractive price — or opt for superior clarity and brilliance — without paying the natural diamond premium. It’s a new kind of luxury, demanded by those who want to optimize their budgets for smaller, meaningful occasions.' The inclusion of fancy-colored diamonds — an alternative to rare, high-value natural colored diamonds that can cost up to $2 million per carat — is especially innovative, as producing consistent, vibrant colors in lab-grown diamonds remains technically challenging. Valquère’s suppliers focus on precise color control, stable growth conditions, and achieving significant stone sizes to enable reliable blue and pink diamond offerings. Consumer adoption will determine whether these colored diamonds gain broad appeal — analysts do not expect them to achieve investment value like natural counterparts. The company purchases lab-grown diamonds directly from producers, selecting only F and E color grades with VS1 and VVS2 clarity. 'Our heritage in investment-grade diamonds and fine jewelry ensures our products have undergone rigorous research and development,' concludes Boelens. 'We only offer the finest — because the people behind this brand are not newcomers to this field.'

article_content: In a fierce two-day battle in southeastern Afghanistan’s Paktika province, U.S. and Afghan forces clashed with insurgents emerging from hidden bunkers and caves, resulting in the death of Army Master Sgt. Benjamin A. Stevenson — one of the few fatalities ever recorded among elite special operations units. Stevenson, a 36-year-old veteran from Texas on his 10th combat deployment, was killed after being evacuated from the battlefield. The operation began as a nighttime strike targeting a Haqqani network encampment, where nearly 80 foreign fighters — primarily Arab and Chechen militants smuggled in from Pakistan — were neutralized. But as daylight revealed the terrain, waves of additional insurgents launched surprise attacks from underground positions, forcing U.S. commanders to call in reinforcements multiple times. Military officials described the incident as a rare window into the high-risk missions carried out by secretive units often likened to Delta Force. The presence of so many non-Afghan fighters within the Haqqani network marks a troubling shift, suggesting the group is broadening its reach and capabilities beyond local recruitment, potentially with external support.

Stevenson — uno dei pochi decessi mai registrati tra le unità speciali d'élite. Stevenson, un veterano di 36 anni del Texas in missione di combattimento numero dieci, è deceduto dopo essere stato evacuato dal campo di battaglia. L'operazione era iniziata come un attacco notturno contro un accampamento della rete Haqqani, dove quasi 80 combattenti stranieri — principalmente militanti arabi e ceceni introdotti dal Pakistan — sono stati neutralizzati. Ma quando la luce del giorno ha rivelato il terreno, onde aggiuntive di insorti hanno lanciato attacchi sorpresa da posizioni sotterranee, costringendo i comandanti americani a richiedere rinforzi più volte. Funzionari militari hanno descritto l'incidente come una rara finestra sulle missioni ad alto rischio condotte da unità segrete spesso paragonate alla Delta Force. La presenza di così tanti combattenti non afghani all'interno della rete Haqqani rappresenta un cambiamento preoccupante, suggerendo che il gruppo sta ampliando la sua portata e le sue capacità al di là del reclutamento locale, potenzialmente con sostegno esterno.

article_content: By Eddie Wrenn. PUBLISHED: 07:39 EST, 9 March 2012. | UPDATED: 07:19 EST, 12 March 2012. Powerful data: Wikipedia relies on volunteers to keep its content updated and accurate. It is often said that history is written by the victors—but now, anyone with a web connection—and perhaps an agenda—can shape how they are remembered. Where once politicians relied on rhetoric to sway voters, today they wield the power of the internet—and they’re not shy about using it. The Bureau of Investigative Journalism has uncovered nearly 10,000 instances of individuals within the Houses of Parliament editing Wikipedia articles. Some edits appear to settle old scores—for example, one user added a reference to union leader Bob Crow’s 'massive salary.' Others seem aimed at boosting egos, such as an edit to Labour MP Fabian Hamilton’s page, which claimed he faced 'an unfair, personally targeted campaign from his political opponents who used exaggerated expenses claims and false information to discredit a powerful incumbent who has served Leeds North East for many years.' Some edits attempt to mitigate embarrassment from the 2009 expenses scandal. For instance, the Wikipedia entry for MP Clare Short originally stated she 'admitted that she overclaimed £8,000 worth of expenses on her home and, like many other MPs, claimed it was a mistake and blamed it on Commons officials.' This was rewritten to read: 'She confirmed that in 2006, the fees office had asked her to repay £8,000 because, for three years, they had erroneously paid her full mortgage rather than just the interest.' Contacted by The Independent, Short said her staff were 'angry and protective' about inaccurate entries on her page and acknowledged they may have made the changes—but insisted, 'It certainly wasn’t me. I never look at it. I find it too irritating. The only change I know was made to my page was my grandchildren adding their names.' Other edits are plainly frivolous—especially coming from those entrusted with governing the nation. Examples include edits regarding the legal status of Pringles (crisp or cake?) and updates to the biography of Molly Weasley, a fictional character from the Harry Potter series. The Bureau found that nearly one in six MPs had their Wikipedia pages edited from within Parliament, with dozens of changes seeking to erase or soften allegations tied to the 2009 expenses scandal. All internet users inside Parliament are routed through two known IP addresses, which Wikipedia logs as digital fingerprints. By matching these IPs with Wikipedia’s edit records, the Bureau identified nearly 10,000 edits. One of the most persistent campaigns targeted Joan Ryan, who stepped down as a Labour MP in 2010. In 2009, the Daily Telegraph reported she claimed over £4,500 for renovations to her home in Enfield before designating a flat in south London as her second home. At least ten edits from Parliament sought to remove this information; another twenty attempts—some originating from her constituency—were logged. The effort succeeded: Ryan’s current Wikipedia page no longer mentions her expenses claims. When contacted, Ryan admitted to altering her page: 'I’ve altered it whenever there’s misleading or untrue information placed on it.' Other notable edits include: - A 2008 edit to Andrew Marr’s page referencing a superinjunction—a potentially contemptuous act, as discussing active legal injunctions is illegal. - Seven edits to the 'Laws about Incest' page, listing jurisdictions where it is legal. - A reduction of the estimated number of women forced into sexual slavery by Japan during WWII from 60,000 to 10,000. - An edit to Bob Crow’s page adding the phrase 'massive salary.' - An edit to Chris Huhne’s register of interests removing mention of gold mining companies. - Removal in 2006 of a line stating Huhne was a signatory to a letter expressing no confidence in Charles Kennedy. - Correction of spelling errors on the Pringles page regarding its legal classification. - A user corrected the spelling of Ken Livingstone’s last name from 'T*atface' to 'Livingstone.' - An edit to The Lord of the Rings page calling it '12 hours of utter tripe about some little bender running around trying to find a ring with his equally benderish mates.' - Michael Fabricant was briefly listed among 'Notable DJs.' Ryan maintained that redesignating her second home did not constitute 'flipping,' as she never claimed expenses for renovations to her London flat. In another case, six attempts were made between 2006 and 2007 to delete a quote from MP Philip Davies to the Sun newspaper: 'If there’s anyone who should f**k off it’s the Muslims who do this sort of thing.' Each time, other users restored the passage. When asked, Davies denied involvement: 'No, it certainly was not me... I do not care what people say about me—let alone care about what it might say about me on Wikipedia.' A passage detailing how Chris Kelly emailed colleagues to ask them to hire his sister also vanished. He was unavailable for comment. Jon Davies, CEO of Wikimedia UK, welcomed greater participation from MPs but noted many edits were unwelcome. 'We would welcome any MPs who want to become editors,' he said. 'However, dozens of parliamentarians have been warned—or blocked—for vandalism.' In July 2009, one administrator issued a final warning: 'This is the last warning you will receive for your disruptive edits. The next time you disrupt Wikipedia, as you did to Eric Clapton, you will be blocked from editing.' This investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism on behalf of The Independent.

Dati potenti: Wikipedia dipende dai volontari per mantenere il suo contenuto aggiornato e accurato. Una volta i politici si affidavano alla retorica per influenzare gli elettori; oggi esercitano il potere di internet—e non esitano ad usarlo. L'Ufficio di Giornalismo Investigativo ha scoperto quasi 10.000 casi di persone all'interno delle Camere del Parlamento che hanno modificato articoli di Wikipedia. Alcune modifiche sembrano voler risolvere vecchi conti—per esempio, un utente ha aggiunto un riferimento al 'salario enorme' del sindacalista Bob Crow. Altre sembrano mirare a gratificare l'ego, come la modifica alla pagina di Fabian Hamilton, deputato laburista, che affermava di aver subito 'una campagna ingiusta e personalmente mirata da parte dei suoi avversari politici, che hanno usato richieste di spese esagerate e informazioni false per screditare un potente incaricato che ha servito Leeds North East per molti anni.' Alcune modifiche cercano di ridurre l'imbarazzo causato dallo scandalo delle spese del 2009. Per esempio, la pagina Wikipedia di Clare Short originariamente diceva che aveva 'ammesso di aver richiesto £8.000 in spese eccessive per la sua casa e, come molti altri deputati, ha attribuito l'errore agli ufficiali della Camera dei Comuni.' Questo è stato riscritto come: 'Ha confermato che nel 2006 l'ufficio spese le aveva chiesto di restituire £8.000 perché, per tre anni, avevano erroneamente pagato l'intero mutuo invece che solo gli interessi.' Contattata dal The Independent, Short ha detto che il suo staff era 'arrabbiato e protettivo' riguardo alle voci inaccurate sulla sua pagina e ha ammesso che potrebbero essere stati loro a fare le modifiche—ma ha insistito: 'Non sono stata io. Non guardo mai la pagina. Mi infastidisce troppo. L'unica modifica che so essere stata fatta alla mia pagina è stata l'aggiunta dei nomi dei miei nipoti.' Altre modifiche sono semplicemente frivole—soprattutto se provengono da chi è incaricato di governare il paese. Esempi includono modifiche sullo status legale dei Pringles (cracker o torta?) e aggiornamenti alla biografia di Molly Weasley, un personaggio immaginario di Harry Potter. Tutti gli utenti internet all'interno del Parlamento sono instradati attraverso due indirizzi IP noti, che Wikipedia registra come impronte digitali digitali. Abbinando questi IP ai registri delle modifiche di Wikipedia, l'Ufficio ha identificato quasi 10.000 modifiche. Una delle campagne più persistenti ha colpito Joan Ryan, che ha lasciato il ruolo di deputata laburista nel 2010. Almeno dieci modifiche provenienti dal Parlamento hanno cercato di rimuovere queste informazioni; altre venti tentativi—alcuni provenienti dal suo collegio elettorale—sono stati registrati. L'operazione ha avuto successo: la pagina attuale di Ryan non menziona più le sue spese parlamentari. Contattata, Ryan ha ammesso di aver modificato la sua pagina: 'Ho modificato ogni volta che c'erano informazioni fuorvianti o false inserite.' Altre modifiche notevoli includono: - Una modifica del 2008 alla pagina di Andrew Marr che citava un'ingiunzione sovraordinata—un atto potenzialmente di contumacia, poiché discutere di ingiunzioni legali attive è illegale. - Sette modifiche alla pagina 'Leggi sull'incesto,' che elencano le giurisdizioni dove è legale. - Una riduzione del numero stimato di donne costrette in schiavitù sessuale dal Giappone durante la Seconda Guerra Mondiale da 60.000 a 10.000. - Una modifica alla pagina di Bob Crow che aggiunge la frase 'salario enorme.' - Una modifica al registro degli interessi di Chris Huhne che rimuove il riferimento alle aziende minerarie d'oro. - Rimozione nel 2006 di una frase che indicava Huhne come firmatario di una lettera di sfiducia verso Charles Kennedy. - Correzione di errori ortografici sulla pagina dei Pringles riguardo alla loro classificazione legale. - Un utente ha corretto la grafia del cognome di Ken Livingstone da 'T*atface' a 'Livingstone.' - Una modifica alla pagina de Il Signore degli Anelli che la definisce '12 ore di puro trippa su un piccolo bender che gira cercando un anello insieme ai suoi compagni altrettanto bender.' - Michael Fabricant è stato brevemente incluso nell'elenco dei 'DJ notevoli.' Ryan ha sostenuto che il cambio di residenza secondaria non costituiva un 'trucco,' poiché non aveva mai richiesto spese per ristrutturazioni nel suo appartamento londinese. In un altro caso, sei tentativi tra il 2006 e il 2007 hanno cercato di cancellare una citazione del deputato Philip Davies al Sun: 'Se c'è qualcuno che dovrebbe f**k off, sono i musulmani che fanno questo genere di cose.' Ogni volta, altri utenti hanno ripristinato il passaggio. Quando interrogato, Davies ha negato qualsiasi coinvolgimento: 'No, certamente non sono stato io... Non mi importa cosa la gente dice di me—né cosa potrebbe dire su di me su Wikipedia.' Un passaggio che descriveva come Chris Kelly avesse inviato email ai colleghi per chiedere loro di assumere sua sorella è scomparso. Non è stato raggiungibile per commenti. Jon Davies, CEO di Wikimedia UK, ha accolto con favore una maggiore partecipazione dei deputati ma ha notato che molte modifiche erano indesiderate. 'Accogliamo con favore qualsiasi deputato che voglia diventare un editore,' ha detto. 'Tuttavia, decine di parlamentari sono stati avvertiti—o bloccati—per vandalismo.' Nel luglio 2009, un amministratore ha emesso un ultimo avvertimento: 'Questo è l'ultimo avvertimento che riceverai per le tue modifiche disruptive. La prossima volta che disturberai Wikipedia, come hai fatto con Eric Clapton, sarai bloccato dalla modifica.' Questa indagine è stata condotta dall'Ufficio di Giornalismo Investigativo per conto del The Independent.

article_content: Robin van Persie is expected to recover in time to face Manchester City in next week’s high-stakes derby, despite being stretchered off during Manchester United’s 3-0 Champions League win over Olympiacos on Wednesday night. The Dutch striker delivered a stunning hat-trick—scoring from a penalty, a close-range finish, and a curling free-kick—to help United overturn a 2-0 first-leg deficit and advance 3-2 on aggregate. His night ended prematurely after a late challenge from Olympiacos defender Kostas Manolas, prompting concern among fans and teammates alike. However, manager David Moyes quickly downplayed fears, stating the injury appeared minor, possibly just a knee to the back. While Van Persie’s availability for Saturday’s Premier League match against West Ham remains uncertain, sources indicate he is on track to feature against City on Tuesday. Further medical assessments are scheduled for Thursday, but early signs are highly encouraging. Moyes praised Van Persie’s performance, calling it a rare and brilliant feat in Champions League football. Wayne Rooney, who assisted two goals, was seen offering support as Van Persie received treatment on the pitch.

Il centravanti olandese ha realizzato una tripletta straordinaria—segna da rigore, con un colpo ravvicinato e un tiro libero curvato—per aiutare la squadra a ribaltare uno svantaggio di 2-0 dal primo incontro e avanzare con un punteggio aggregato di 3-2. La sua serata è terminata prematuramente dopo un intervento tardivo del difensore dell'Olympiacos Kostas Manolas, suscitando preoccupazione tra i tifosi e i compagni di squadra. Tuttavia, l'allenatore David Moyes ha subito minimizzato le paure, dichiarando che l'infortunio sembrava lieve, probabilmente solo un calcio alla schiena. Mentre la sua disponibilità per la partita di Premier League di sabato contro il West Ham rimane incerta, fonti indicano che è in rotta per disputare la gara contro la City martedì. Ulteriori accertamenti medici sono previsti per giovedì, ma i primi segnali sono molto incoraggianti. Moyes ha elogiato la prestazione di Van Persie, definendola un raro e brillante traguardo nel calcio della Champions League. Wayne Rooney, che ha fornito due assist, è stato visto mentre offriva sostegno a Van Persie mentre riceveva cure sul campo.

article_content: At 30,000 feet above the Earth, Dr. Betty Gikonyo’s life took a turn she never expected. Years ago, she was flying from Kenya to the U.S. with her husband and three kids—her husband was headed to Minneapolis for a medical fellowship. But before takeoff, the family was asked to help an 18-year-old boy traveling alone for urgent heart treatment. Everything seemed fine until, mid-flight, the teenager began struggling to breathe and foamed at the mouth. Fortunately, Gikonyo had the right meds on hand and sprang into action, stabilizing him in the cramped cabin. After a brief layover in Brussels, they continued their journey. That moment stayed with her. 'It hit me,' she says, 'that you don’t need to know someone to feel responsible for their wellbeing.' Back in Kenya, she channeled that feeling into action. Today, she’s one of the country’s top pediatric cardiologists. She co-founded the Heart to Heart Foundation to fund life-saving surgeries for kids who can’t afford them, and arranged medical flights to get children overseas when needed. But her biggest milestone came in 2006: opening Karen Hospital just outside Nairobi—a dream she’d held for twenty years—to give children the care they deserve, right at home.

Ma prima del decollo, alla famiglia fu chiesto di aiutare un ragazzo di 18 anni che viaggiava da solo per un trattamento urgente per una malattia cardiaca. Tutto sembrava sotto controllo fino a quando, in volo, il ragazzo ha iniziato ad avere difficoltà respiratorie e a schiumare dalla bocca. Fortunatamente, Gikonyo aveva i farmaci giusti e ha agito immediatamente, stabilizzandolo nella cabina affollata. Dopo una breve sosta a Bruxelles, hanno proseguito il viaggio. Quell’istante l’ha segnata profondamente. 'Mi sono resa conto,' dice, 'che non devi conoscere qualcuno per sentirti responsabile del suo benessere.' Tornata in Kenya, ha trasformato quel senso di responsabilità in azione. Oggi è uno dei principali cardiologi pediatrici del paese. Ha fondato insieme ad altri la Heart to Heart Foundation per finanziare interventi salvavita per bambini che non possono permetterseli, e ha organizzato voli medici per portare i bambini all’estero quando necessario. Ma il suo traguardo più grande è arrivato nel 2006: l’apertura dell’Ospedale Karen, appena fuori Nairobi—un sogno che coltivava da vent’anni—per offrire ai bambini le cure che meritano, proprio a casa loro.

article_content: For more than half a year, a 19-year-old woman endured horrific abuse at the hands of her relative, Timothy Jay Vafeades, a trucker who lured her away from Florida under false promises of work and financial independence. What began as a trip to help with his trucking business quickly turned into a nightmare of captivity. After arriving in Utah, she awoke to find him sexually assaulting her in their shared bed. From that moment, her freedom vanished. Vafeades confiscated her ID and Social Security card, forbade her from using public restrooms or showering alone, and demanded she hold his hand at all times—even punishing her with blows if she so much as made eye contact with another person. She estimates he struck her 20 to 30 times. One night, desperate and terrified, she found a razor blade and considered using it to fight back—or end her life. But she believed escape was impossible, so she threw it away. The abuse didn’t stop. Vafeades, who called himself a 'master' and wore metal bracelets he called 'slave bracelets' to beat her, also obsessed over vampires. He had custom-made dentures shaped like fangs and even filed down some of her own teeth. When police stopped his truck during a routine weight check in Minnesota, they discovered the protection order against him and realized the woman riding with him was his victim. He now faces charges of kidnapping, false imprisonment, and domestic abuse. Bond has been set at $1 million. Prosecutors say the case is among the most disturbing they’ve seen.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. If Californians thought they had it rough dealing with the drought plaguing the state, they now face a new concern: the dry spell is driving more skunks out of the woods and into residential areas in search of food and water. The issue is especially pronounced in El Dorado County, located east of Sacramento in California’s historic Gold Country. Jennifer Hamburg of the El Dorado County Animal Control Division told CBS Sacramento that in a typical year, her department receives five to seven reports of skunk sightings. But in just the past two months, she has received seven such reports—many occurring in residential neighborhoods. While skunks are generally harmless if left undisturbed, Hamburg noted that drought conditions appear to be making some individuals more aggressive. 'The calls we’ve received recently suggest a noticeable increase in aggressive behavior,' she said. 'They’re chasing after people’s dogs.' Rabid skunks often display signs such as difficulty walking or drinking, and appear disoriented. Pet owners are strongly advised to ensure their animals are vaccinated against rabies, especially if they spend time outdoors. The drought shows no sign of abating. According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), California just experienced its warmest and third-driest winter on record. article_content: A large-scale analysis of over a million restaurant reviews from 2002 to 2011 reveals that the weather on the day a review is written can strongly influence its tone. Researchers Saeideh Bakhshi, Partha Kanuparthy, and Eric Gilbert examined data from 840,000 eateries and found that diners are more likely to leave glowing reviews when the temperature is between 70 and 100 degrees Fahrenheit on a sunny day. Conversely, reviews penned during extreme heat, freezing temperatures, rain, or snow tend to be noticeably harsher. The team suggests this isn’t about the food — it’s about mood. Science has long shown that sunlight and mild temperatures boost emotional well-being, and that positivity often spills over into how people rate their experiences. Interestingly, summer months like July and August, despite being popular dining seasons, consistently yield lower ratings, possibly because extreme heat makes people irritable. The study also uncovered geographic patterns: restaurants in the Northeast and along the Pacific Coast receive far more reviews than those in the South and Midwest. This gap, researchers believe, correlates with higher education levels and greater demographic diversity in states like California, Washington, and Oregon — areas that also lean politically liberal. In urban centers, customers are more tolerant of delays and prefer delivery options, while in smaller towns, takeout is favored and service standards are judged more critically. Additionally, neighborhoods where over half the residents hold college degrees produce nearly three times as many reviews as areas with minimal college graduation rates. The researchers point to earlier findings that weather even affects tipping behavior and server morale. Ultimately, the study reminds us that even passionate food lovers aren’t immune to the subtle power of the elements. As one researcher put it: 'You can serve the perfect meal and offer flawless service — but you can’t change the forecast.'

article_content: In December 2012, eight-week-old Hanna Faheem passed away at Sheffield Children’s Hospital after being treated for respiratory symptoms. Her mother, Naseem Akhtar, had been told her daughter had Edwards’ Syndrome, a rare and often fatal genetic condition, and was preparing for a shortened life. But after Hanna’s death, police revealed that she may have received a fatal overdose of morphine — 3.5 milligrams instead of the prescribed 0.35mg. The error, reportedly detected an hour after administration, led to the suspension of three hospital staff members. Just hours after Hanna’s funeral was planned at a local mosque, South Yorkshire Police arrived at the family’s home and halted the ceremony to recover her body for a post-mortem. Ms. Akhtar, devastated, said she had accepted her daughter’s limited prognosis but never imagined the hospital’s actions could have cut their time together even shorter. 'They never told us what happened,' she said. 'We were allowed to bury her — then they took her away.' The hospital confirmed it was cooperating with police, but declined to comment further due to the ongoing investigation. An inquest has since been opened. The case has sparked widespread concern about medication safety protocols in pediatric units and the ethical obligation of hospitals to communicate critical errors to grieving families.

article_content: Erika Harold was everything the Republican Party claims to want in a candidate: a Harvard Law graduate, former Miss America, and a speaker at the 2004 Republican National Convention. Yet when she decided to challenge incumbent Rep. Rodney Davis in Illinois’ 13th District, she didn’t find allies—she found walls. Despite her pedigree, party officials refused to share voter data, discouraged her from running, and even suggested she pursue a different office. At campaign events, donors were quietly warned off. Meanwhile, local GOP leaders made headlines for openly racist and misogynistic remarks. Jim Allen, then-chair of the Montgomery County GOP, called her a 'street walker' and mocked her as the 'love child of the D.N.C.'—comments that sparked national outrage and led to his resignation. Harold wasn’t just losing a primary; she was being erased by a party that says it values diversity but treats women of color as outsiders. Her loss—55% to 41%—wasn’t just a defeat. It was a signal. While the GOP launched programs like Project GROW and '14 in 14' to recruit more women, the reality on the ground tells a different story. Contrast Harold’s experience with that of Mia Love, the Haitian-American Republican who won her Utah seat in 2014. Love got early endorsements, robust fundraising, and full party backing. Why? Because she ran in an open seat. Harold ran against an incumbent—and the party protects incumbents, especially men. Studies from Rutgers show Republican women are far less likely than Democrats to run or win primaries, partly because most districts are so polarized that moderate voices get crushed. Add to that the fact that conservative women lack powerful donor networks like EMILY’s List, and the odds become nearly impossible. Even Sarah Palin’s SarahPAC and smaller groups like SHE PAC are trying to fill the gap—but they’re fighting an uphill battle against institutional inertia. Former Senator Olympia Snowe put it plainly: the GOP isn’t leaning in—it’s standing still. Harold, now practicing law in Illinois, says it clearly: without real support—from party infrastructure, funding, and culture—women like her won’t just lose elections. They’ll stop running altogether.

article_content: In a dramatic finish at Doncaster Racecourse, Encke surged past the heavily favored Camelot to claim victory in the St Leger Stakes, dashing hopes of England’s first Triple Crown winner in over four decades. Camelot, who had already conquered the 2,000 Guineas and the Epsom Derby, was aiming to match the legendary Nijinsky by sweeping all three Classic races in a single season. But on Saturday, it was Encke — ridden by French jockey Mickael Barzalona in his debut St Leger — who stole the spotlight. Barzalona described the ride as surprisingly smooth, saying he felt confident throughout. The race unfolded tactically, with pacemaker Dartford setting a steady tempo while Camelot lingered toward the back. As the field entered the final straight, Joseph O’Brien struggled to find a clear path for Camelot, giving Encke the crucial breathing room he needed. Even when Camelot finally found room and launched his challenge, he couldn’t close the gap fully, finishing just three-quarters of a length behind. The win marks Sheikh Mohammed’s sixth St Leger triumph, moving him into second place among all-time owners of the race. Meanwhile, trainer Aiden O’Brien’s dream of becoming the first to win all five English Classics in one year — including the fillies’ races — came to an end. With his Triple Crown bid over, Camelot’s next outing may now be the prestigious Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe in France, where he’ll seek redemption on an international stage.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. PUBLISHED: 19:59 EST, 16 September 2012. | UPDATED: 18:00 EST, 17 September 2012. The families of two British soldiers killed by a man disguised as an Afghan police officer have paid tribute to their loved ones. Married father-of-two Sergeant Gareth Thursby, 29, and Private Thomas Wroe, 18, were shot dead in the Nahr-e Saraj district of Helmand province on Saturday, 15 September 2012. Both served in the 3rd Battalion, The Yorkshire Regiment (Duke of Wellington's). Defence sources said the men were killed at a checkpoint when a man pretending to be an injured local Afghan policeman approached them, then opened fire. Sergeant Thursby, from Skipton, North Yorkshire, is survived by his wife Louise and their two children, Joshua and Ruby. His wife said: 'Gareth was the love of my life. He was an amazing husband and father—happy, full of life, kind-hearted, with a passion for his work and family. He was brave, hardworking, a loving husband and devoted father. Our hero.' Private Wroe, who joined the Army in September 2010, was deployed to Afghanistan on 1 July, shortly after his 18th birthday. He is survived by his parents, Michael and Claire, and sister Demi, from Holmfirth, West Yorkshire. His family said in a statement: 'Our son Thomas was a brave young soldier, loved by his family, girlfriend, and friends. We can't believe you’ve been taken so soon from us. You will always be in our hearts forever. You lit up every room with your smile and bubbly personality. Our world will be duller without you. We are so proud of you, son—for all you achieved and every special thing you gave us. We will always love you, Tom.' Sergeant Thursby, who had previously served in Kosovo and Iraq, was nicknamed 'Bull' for his strength and confidence. His commanding officer, Lieutenant Colonel Zachary Stenning, said: 'He was admired and deeply respected by his soldiers and peers for his soldiering skills, physical strength, and forthright honesty. Utterly professional, his standards were legendary.' He added: 'A few weeks ago, I heard he’d asked his platoon to call him Dad during the tour. That’s how he saw himself—a father figure to 30 men and women enduring grueling operations in Helmand.' Private Wroe’s company commander, Major Finlay Bibby, praised his professionalism and spirit: 'His confidence, sense of humour, and ever-present smile made him hugely popular and fun to be with. He was an extremely talented soldier fulfilling his dream by serving with the same battalion his father had served in. I have no doubt he would have achieved great things in the Army.' The Ministry of Defence confirmed an investigation is underway. An MoD spokesperson said: 'It is with sadness that the Ministry of Defence must announce the deaths of two soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, The Yorkshire Regiment, on Saturday, 15 September 2012.' Major Laurence Roche of Task Force Helmand called the loss 'deep,' adding: 'Everyone serving within Task Force Helmand wants to send our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of these soldiers.' These deaths come amid a violent period in Afghanistan. On Friday, 14 September, Lance Corporal Duane Groom, 32, of the 1st Battalion Grenadier Guards, died after his vehicle struck a roadside bomb. The MoD confirmed these incidents were unrelated to the earlier attack on Camp Bastion, which killed two U.S. Marines and damaged multiple aircraft. Attackers at Camp Bastion used automatic weapons, rocket-propelled grenades, and suicide vests. The Taliban claimed responsibility, stating the attack was retaliation for an amateur film mocking the Prophet Muhammad and the presence of Prince Harry on base. Prince Harry, who turned 28 on Saturday, is on his second tour and remains scheduled to begin flying Apache missions. His deployment will not be shortened. The latest fatalities bring the total number of UK service members killed in Afghanistan since operations began in October 2001 to 430. In a separate incident, an Afghan police officer opened fire on NATO troops at a remote checkpoint, killing four U.S. service members before fleeing, according to Afghan and international officials.

article_content: A Michigan teacher gave fifth-grade students O’Doul’s — a beverage labeled 'non-alcoholic' — during a lesson on Colonial-era drinks, unaware that it contains 0.5% alcohol. The teacher, whose identity has not been disclosed, allowed students at Hyatt Elementary School in Linden to sample the drink after a student brought it to class to represent historical ale. Though legally classified as non-alcoholic under U.S. standards (≤0.5% ABV), O’Doul’s still contains trace alcohol, making its distribution to minors a potential misdemeanor under Michigan law. Liquor Control Commission spokeswoman Andrea Miller confirmed such actions could be prosecuted, though no charges have been filed. Superintendent Ed Koledo described the teacher as 'very responsible' and emphasized no harm was intended. He explained the intent was to illustrate that water was often unsafe in the 1700s, making low-alcohol fermented beverages common. 'We talked to the teacher and said this was an inappropriate choice,' Koledo told the Flint Journal. 'There were far better options to represent colonial-era drinks.' Students were not forced to taste the beverage; however, three took bottles home. Principal Vicki Malkaravage notified parents via letter, noting the teacher believed the product was safe due to its labeling. Neither the student nor the teacher has been disciplined, and school officials stated no complaints were received. The matter was monitored the following day and deemed inactive.

L'insegnante, la cui identità non è stata rivelata, ha consentito agli studenti della Hyatt Elementary School di Linden di assaggiare la bevanda dopo che uno studente l'aveva portata a scuola per rappresentare la birra storica. La portavoce della Liquor Control Commission, Andrea Miller, ha confermato che tali azioni possono essere perseguite penalmente, sebbene non siano state presentate accuse. Il sovrintendente Ed Koledo ha descritto l'insegnante come 'molto responsabile' e ha sottolineato che non c'era alcuna intenzione di causare danno. Ha spiegato che l'obiettivo era mostrare che nell'epoca coloniale l'acqua era spesso contaminata, rendendo comuni le bevande fermentate a basso contenuto alcolico. 'Abbiamo parlato con l'insegnante e le abbiamo fatto presente che si trattava di una scelta inadeguata,' ha detto Koledo al Flint Journal. 'C'erano opzioni molto più appropriate per rappresentare le bevande dell'epoca coloniale.' Gli studenti non sono stati obbligati ad assaggiare la bevanda; tuttavia, tre di loro hanno portato a casa una bottiglia. La preside Vicki Malkaravage ha informato i genitori tramite lettera, precisando che l'insegnante riteneva il prodotto sicuro grazie all'etichetta. Né lo studente né l'insegnante sono stati sanzionati, e le autorità scolastiche hanno affermato che nessuna reclamo è stato presentato. La situazione è stata monitorata il giorno successivo e considerata chiusa.

article_content: Already wealthy from the inheritance left by his comedy legend father, Adam Barker has celebrated a new financial windfall. According to reports, the 45-year-old son of Ronnie Barker sold his London home for £550,000 — more than five times the £100,000 his father paid for it in 2001. The property, located in Ealing, was the site where Barker downloaded 1,675 pornographic images, predominantly depicting young boys, on his computer. Its value surged while he was fleeing bail and later incarcerated. Following his 2003 arrest at the property, Barker rented it out to tenants during the eight years he evaded prosecution. After pleading guilty to 20 counts of possessing indecent images of children — including two classified at Level 5, the highest severity — he received a 12-month sentence in 2022. He was released after just 14 weeks. Judge Rosa Dean stated during sentencing: 'Your offences contributed to the degradation and continued abuse of children. This wasn't a one-off offense.' Barker has never publicly commented on, apologized for, or explained his crimes. He did not attend his father’s funeral in 2005, nor claim his share of the £275,000 tax-free inheritance left by Ronnie; instead, the funds were held in trust until his return. His largest financial gain came after his mother Joy’s death in 2011, when her estate — including the bulk of Ronnie’s assets — was valued at £6.5 million. Alongside his sister Charlotte, 52, and brother Larry, 54, Adam is a joint heir to royalties from 'The Two Ronnies' through Handles For Forks Ltd, a company established to manage those earnings. As a registered sex offender, Barker is legally required to disclose his full-time address. Official records list a correspondence address in the Cotswolds, but authorities believe he does not reside there.

article_content: Passengers on an Etihad Airways flight from Melbourne to Abu Dhabi endured a harrowing journey after a mystery individual set five fires in the aircraft's lavatories. The Boeing 777-300ER made an emergency landing in Jakarta after the first two fires broke out. Following a security check, passengers were cleared to continue — only for three more fires to ignite during the next leg of the flight, roughly two hours before arriving in Abu Dhabi. Sarah Jeffery, one of the passengers, recounted waking to blaring alarms and flashing red lights, seeing flames in a toilet waste bin as crew swiftly extinguished them. 'It was very smoky — the entire cabin felt filled with smoke,' she told The Age. Another passenger, professional golfer Caroline Martens, described the experience on Instagram as 'trying to have someone set the plane on fire twice, land in Jakarta, return to the plane, then have the same person set three more fires mid-air with nowhere to land.' She noted that after the initial landing, passengers were told they couldn't disembark due to visa restrictions, forcing them back onto a plane with an unknown arsonist still aboard. Flight attendants instructed everyone to remain seated and banned toilet use for the remainder of the journey. Meals were suspended, and passengers reported being unable to eat or drink for nearly 19 hours — including those requiring medication for chronic conditions like diabetes. Cabin crew emphasized that due to cabin pressure, fires must be extinguished within 90 seconds to prevent catastrophic failure. Upon arrival in Abu Dhabi, police interviewed passengers in small groups but made no arrests. Reports suggest investigators are looking into a female passenger, though no official confirmation has been released. Etihad Airways stated that authorities are continuing their investigation and that further updates will follow.

article_content: Thirteen people were killed and 90 others wounded in violent clashes between Coptic Christians and Muslims in Cairo, according to Egypt’s state-run television. The unrest erupted on Tuesday after Coptic demonstrators took to the streets to protest the burning of a church in Helwan province last week. Initially, Egypt’s Health Minister, Dr. Ashraf Hatem, reported nine deaths; however, Coptic Church spokesman Father Abdelmaseeh Baseet later confirmed six fatalities — all Christians — with the total rising to 13. The Egyptian military has launched an investigation into the violence. Mohamed Askar, a military spokesperson, warned that anyone involved in inciting sectarian hatred or committing acts of violence would face prosecution under the full force of the law. The church arson is believed to have originated from a personal feud between a Muslim and a Coptic family. Tensions between Egypt’s Muslim majority and its Coptic minority have intensified in recent months. On New Year’s Day, a bombing at a church in Alexandria killed 23 people; the Palestinian Islamic Army, linked to al Qaeda, claimed responsibility — marking the deadliest attack on Christians in Egypt in years. Just ten days later, a gunman attacked a train, killing one Christian and wounding five others. In January, a man was convicted for his role in a prior attack on a Coptic church. Coptic Christians constitute approximately 9% of Egypt’s 80 million population. Their faith traces back to the Apostle Mark, who brought Christianity to Egypt, and diverged from mainstream Christianity in the fifth century over theological differences regarding the nature of Christ’s divinity.

article_content: Melvin Morse, a 60-year-old former pediatrician and once-famous television personality, is facing trial in Delaware on charges of child endangerment and assault. Prosecutors allege he subjected his stepdaughter to abusive hair-washing incidents by forcibly holding her head under running water — a practice he claims was merely an attempt to clean her hair after she refused baths at age 8. Morse, known nationally in the 1990s for his appearances on 'Larry King Live,' 'The Oprah Winfrey Show,' and 'Unsolved Mysteries' — often discussing his research into children’s near-death experiences — denies any intent to harm. He insists he never tortured the girl and even treated her the same as his biological daughter, giving both children equal Christmas gifts. The girl, now 12, and her mother, Pauline Morse, however, testify that these hair-washing incidents were used as punishment. Pauline described witnessing Morse hold the girl’s head under running water without soap, leaving the child coughing and shaking. She admitted she repeatedly ignored the abuse out of fear and a desire not to undermine him. Pauline Morse pleaded guilty last year to misdemeanor child endangerment for failing to protect her daughter. She also testified that Morse dragged the girl by her ankle across a gravel driveway, starved her, and restricted bathroom access. The girl fled the home in July 2012 and reported the abuse to police, triggering the criminal investigation. If convicted on all charges, Morse could face over 20 years in prison. His medical license has already been suspended. Despite the allegations, he maintains he is a doctor and intends to return to practice. The trial, now in its eighth day, continues with testimony from both sides as jurors weigh conflicting narratives of care versus cruelty.

article_content: A teenager hanged himself at the same location where his father — who had shot his wife following allegations of an affair — later took his own life, a highly emotional inquest heard yesterday. Before his death, 16-year-old Jack Williams sent a text message to his deceased father: 'I love you so much, Da.' Jack had struggled to cope with the bitter breakdown of his parents’ marriage, which ended when 46-year-old Darren Williams burst into his estranged wife’s hairdressing salon and shot her at close range with a sawn-off shotgun. Darren Williams, 46, was found dead after fatally shooting his wife, Rachel, 41, following claims she was having an affair with a solicitor. Despite sustaining a severe leg injury, Rachel wrestled the gun away from Darren — a 6ft 7in, 20-stone former bouncer — who fled the scene. Jack’s body was discovered in nearby woodland five weeks later. He had visited the site where his father’s ashes had been scattered. During the inquest in Newport, South Wales, Jack’s final text message was read aloud: 'I hope where you are, you can see this message and know that I love you more than anything in this world. I really do hope you are at peace, and I will definitely see you one day. I really hope it comes soon because I don’t know how long I can live without you.' The inquest revealed Jack had tried to remain neutral during his parents’ separation. However, relations between the two sides of the family deteriorated sharply after the shooting. Tensions erupted in court: insults were exchanged, police were called, and two men were removed after threats of violence. Coroner David Bowen urged the court to respect Jack’s memory. Rachel Williams did not attend the hearing but issued a statement: 'Jack was trying to build an equal relationship with me and his father. When he saw me in hospital, he said, 'I don’t know why he’d do it.' We stayed in touch by text and phone.' However, the inquest also heard Rachel had texted Jack: 'Pack your bags and go and live with the hypocrites,' referring to her husband’s family. Jack then moved in with his father’s sister, Rachael. Rachael’s partner, Wayne Davies, described Jack as 'a remarkable young boy who showed so much courage, dignity, and respect — wise beyond his years. He was a credit to both his mother and father. But the enormity of the situation was too much for him.' Jack’s best friend, Alistair Yates, said: 'On the day Jack died, he said he was going to visit his dad’s ashes. He wanted to be alone. There was no indication he intended to take his own life.' Coroner David Bowen recorded a verdict of suicide, stating: 'This is such a tragic death — his death should never have occurred.'

article_content: An Indian airline has proposed what may be one of the most economically driven justifications yet for hiring predominantly female cabin crew — weight reduction to save fuel and operating costs. While some airlines openly acknowledge hiring flight attendants for aesthetic appeal, budget carrier GoAir told The Times of India it plans to increase the proportion of female cabin crew in future hires because, on average, women weigh 15–20 kilograms less than men. The airline estimates each additional kilogram onboard adds Rs3 ($0.05) to fuel costs per flying hour, and the new hiring strategy could save up to $500,000 annually. A GoAir spokesperson denied to CNN that the company has implemented a gender-biased recruitment policy. However, he confirmed that GoAir’s current male-to-female cabin crew ratio of 40:60 is among the most male-heavy in India’s aviation industry. He also stated the airline intends to shift this ratio closer to the industry standard of 30% male and 70% female. Additional weight-saving measures are underway: the size of in-flight magazines has been reduced, and potable water tanks are no longer filled to full capacity, since only 35–40% of the water is typically consumed. The policy applies only to future hires; GoAir’s existing 130 male cabin crew members (out of 330 total) remain unaffected. The airline expects to hire approximately 2,000 flight attendants and pilots over the next seven years. Fuel efficiency remains a top priority for airlines, as fuel accounts for one-third to half of total operating expenses. Last year, Samoa Air became the world’s first airline to charge passengers based on their weight — a model some economists argue is the fairest and most logical pricing method. The debate continues: Is this sensible cost-cutting, smart marketing, or workplace discrimination?

article_content: For the first time in history, more than half of all Americans now own a smartphone rather than a basic phone — a milestone confirmed by a recent report from Chetan Sharma Consulting. With the U.S. population at roughly 312 million, this means over 150 million people are using smartphones. In the second quarter of 2012, 70% of all phones sold were either iPhones or Android devices, with Android leading in unit sales — even though Apple still earned more revenue and profit per device. Experts believe many U.S. consumers held off buying new phones in anticipation of the upcoming iPhone 5, which was rumored to launch in early September. Meanwhile, smaller carriers like Cricket, MetroPCS, and U.S. Cellular are growing quickly by offering affordable smartphones, helping expand access beyond the big four networks: Verizon, AT&T, Sprint, and T-Mobile. Globally, China stands out as the powerhouse of mobile growth. China Mobile hit a staggering one billion subscriptions in March 2012, becoming the first nation to reach that mark. The secret to its success? Affordable handsets. According to industry analysts, nearly 40% of smartphones shipped in China last year cost under $200, while premium devices priced above $700 made up just 11%. Michael Clendenin of RedTech Advisors notes that the average Chinese consumer — the 'Lao Bai Xing' — prefers mid-range phones priced between $130 and $240. In contrast, Apple’s iPhone sells for around $800 in China — roughly equal to two months’ salary for many urban workers. That’s a steep price when half the country lives on modest incomes. Meanwhile, in the U.S., fewer people are signing long-term contracts: the top four carriers added just 405,000 new contract customers in Q2 2012, less than half the number from the same period the year before. AT&T remains the top seller of iPhones in America, accounting for nearly half of all units. T-Mobile, which doesn’t yet offer the iPhone, is widely expected to begin carrying it soon. The next U.S. wireless market update is due in November, with a global report expected in October.

article_content: Google has launched what it describes as its most advanced voice search system to date. The new features are now available on iOS, following earlier releases on select Android devices and the Google Chrome browser. Google Voice Search is designed to understand the context of user queries, enabling natural follow-up questions on the same topic. For example, after asking about the current weather in Birmingham, a user can simply ask, 'How do I get there?'—without needing to repeat the location. Responses are delivered aloud on smartphones when concise and direct. Google technology expert Michael Valvo said: 'Whether you're plotting the easiest public transport route across London, ordering a drink in Paris in French, or answering a pub quiz question, Google helps you get the information you need, fast.' Other features include turn-by-turn directions based on live traffic data and location-based reminders—for instance, being notified to take out the trash when arriving home or to buy milk when reaching your local supermarket. The system can also identify songs playing nearby—similar to Shazam—and offer options to purchase them via the Google Play Store. Google claims the new voice search is faster and delivers more detailed answers than Apple’s Siri. Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak recently told the BBC he found Android’s search capabilities superior to Siri’s. This upgrade builds on the Hummingbird algorithm introduced in September, which transformed Google’s search engine from keyword matching to understanding full queries like a human would. For example, searching 'Tell me about impressionist artists' now surfaces not just a list of names, but also contextual information about the art movement, links to individual artworks, and filters to explore related styles. Google described Hummingbird as 'the most significant algorithm change in years,' affecting 90% of searches. It began rolling out in August. A special 'Google House' in central London demonstrated practical applications of the technology in everyday scenarios—from cooking to vacation planning. Google also unveiled a new Google+ feature called Auto Awesome, which automatically compiles photos and videos shared on the platform into short video montages. Currently, Auto Awesome Movies is only available on select Android devices running Jelly Bean 4.3, including the Nexus 4, Nexus 7, Nexus 10, HTC One, and Samsung Galaxy S4. Google says it plans to expand access in the future.

article_content: By Katy Winter. The Sound of Music may have been released almost half a century ago, but our fascination with Maria and the Von Trapp family shows no signs of waning. Some of the iconic costumes from the 1965 film — including the outfits Maria fashioned from old curtains — were sold at auction for $1.3 million (£845,000). All seven children’s floral green-and-white costumes were auctioned, along with Maria’s 'Do Re Mi' dress, worn by Julie Andrews as she taught the children to sing. The auction also featured the iconic brown homespun Austrian-style dress Maria wore during the 'Do Re Mi' mountain scene, as well as the lederhosen worn by the Von Trapp boys. The dress, made of heavy wool with a wheat-colored blouse, bears internal labels from 20th Century Fox. Also included were the children’s grey school uniforms from the film’s opening and the outfits worn during the climactic escape scene across the Alps into Switzerland. The film, which won five Oscars in 1966, introduced timeless Rodgers and Hammerstein songs such as 'Edelweiss' and 'My Favorite Things,' launching Julie Andrews into superstardom. In a 2012 interview with Oprah, Andrews admitted she had no idea of the film’s monumental impact, saying, 'It made my career. It was that big of a movie.' The story — of a spirited young nun who unites seven motherless children and their stern father through music, before they flee Nazi-occupied Austria — has endured for generations. Though initially dismissed by critics as overly sentimental, it resonated deeply with audiences worldwide, grossing nearly $300 million at the box office. Its legacy continues through DVD sales, global stage productions, and even a reality TV show, 'How Do You Solve a Problem Like Maria?', which cast a new Maria for a West End revival. The auction, conducted by Profiles in History under Joe Maddalena, was part of a larger Hollywood memorabilia sale that also included a painting of Tara from Gone with the Wind, used in the film’s opening sequence, sold for $270,000 (£175,000).

article_content: It’s not often that lingerie shopping tops the list of priorities for most women — but for Karen Danczuk, it was another chance to capture attention. The 31-year-old Rochdale councillor, wife of Labour MP Simon Danczuk, browsed the aisles of Chantilly, a boutique lingerie shop in Rochdale, selecting a bold red-and-black corset. Moments later, she pulled out her phone and posted a series of selfies on Twitter, captioning one: 'I’m Labour through and through! I even bought the underwear to prove it. KD #imtellingthetruth.' She tagged the store twice and thanked her friend Nicollette North for accompanying her. Danczuk, known for her prolific social media presence and self-proclaimed title as 'Queen of the Selfies,' has built a public persona around candid, often provocative photos — from gym selfies to glamorous nights out. Her 35,000 Twitter followers have grown accustomed to her unfiltered style. This outing followed a pattern: earlier this week, she announced a Valentine’s Day auction, offering a date with her to the highest bidder — a campaign that raised £10,300. She also recently revealed plans to step down from her council seat in the next election to pursue media opportunities, having hired London-based PR firm Ginger Comms. Her actions have drawn sharp criticism. Former Conservative MP Louise Mensch once called her 'the most embarrassing wife in Westminster' and mocked her makeup use. Others question whether such displays are appropriate for a public official. Yet Danczuk remains unfazed. In a separate comment, Danczuk criticized Labour deputy leader Harriet Harman, claiming Harman had told her she was 'too pretty for politics' and should join a girl band instead — a remark Harman has publicly denied. Danczuk’s recent photos, including a pink-and-black ensemble and animal-print lingerie, continue to fuel debate over the boundaries of personal expression in public life.

article_content: Australians have reacted with fury after new laws were passed granting the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) sweeping powers to monitor computer networks. Following the Senate’s approval of the bill by a 44–12 vote—with bipartisan support from Labor—many citizens took to Twitter, adopting the viral 'Hey Girl' trend to voice their discontent under the hashtag #HeyASIO. Critics warn the legislation is dangerously vague: it fails to define what constitutes a 'network,' allowing ASIO to access third-party devices to reach a target system. This effectively opens the entire internet to unchecked surveillance. The law also criminalizes anyone who 'recklessly' discloses information related to a 'special intelligence operation'—a designation that can be unilaterally declared by an authorized ASIO officer. The passage of these controversial anti-terror measures coincides with Australia’s elevated terror alert level and the fatal shooting of teenager Numan Haider in Melbourne. Haider was killed by a Victorian police officer after allegedly stabbing two officers near the Endeavour Hills Police Station. #HeyASIO quickly became the top-trending hashtag on Twitter, reflecting widespread public concern over privacy and state overreach.
